uncited: - **Interval Tree Nodes:** Stored in disk blocks.
**Partition the Interval Tree:** Partition the nodes of the interval tree such that each region fits into one disk block.
Nodes labeled 0 define disk block boundaries.
**Attach Intervals to Nodes:** Attach intervals $I_\eta$ to all interval tree nodes indicating the range of isovalues for which node $\eta$ must be inspected.
**Calculate Expected I/O Time for Interval Tree Blocks ($T_1$):** Compute the expected time to read interval tree disk blocks.
**Calculate Expected I/O Time for Min/Max List Blocks ($T_2$):** Compute the expected time to read min/max list disk blocks.
- **Block Size:** The disk block size must be chosen to accommodate the specific $K_1$ and $K_2$ values.
- **Probability Estimation:** The method relies on probabilistic estimation of isovalue distributions.
A variant that addresses the memory-constrained optimization problem for fixed partitions.
- **Time Complexity:** The expected time to read interval tree blocks is proportional to the sum of probabilities of block intervals.
- **Memory Complexity:** The method is designed for out-of-core operation, storing the interval tree and min/max lists on disk.
Performance depends on disk I/O speed ($\alpha_6$).
- **When Not to Use:** Not suitable for small datasets where in-core methods are faster due to lower overhead.
It addresses the challenge of processing large volume datasets that cannot fit entirely in main memory by partitioning the interval tree and min/max lists into disk blocks.
